_doc:
R16 — TOOLS ARE THINGS YOU BUILD, NOT A GUESS ABOUT YOUR SWORD.

"It appears ranged characters can't harvest materials." They could not, and neither could anybody else in a reliable way, because the tool tier was READ OFF THE WEAPON: js/main.js's old `toolTierFor` matched the weapon's material against a regex — /steel|adamant/ was a Steel Tool, /iron|bronze/ an Iron Tool, anything else 'hands'. A bow is made of yew and string, so an archer was bare-handed at every seam in the game, and a mage with a crystal staff was worse. It also meant nobody could ever ANSWER the question the refusal asked — "you need a Steel Tool" with no tool slot to put one in.

So: a Tool is an item, in its own slot, that you BUILD. One tool is both pickaxe and axe ("The mining tool should be both a pickaxe and axe") because carrying two of a thing that does one job is book-keeping, not a decision. `toolKey` is the row in data/resources.json's `tools` table the item counts as, so every hardness gate, every refusal line and every drill rate goes on reading exactly what it read before.

RARITY IS SPEED AND A LITTLE MORE ("Tools should also be able to come in different rarities that affect mining speed and other things"): `speed` is how fast the progress bar fills, `yield` is the share of extra material that comes off each gather, `reach` is how far from a seam you can stand, and `scan` widens the scanner if you are carrying a better tool when you sweep.

DEVICES are the other two things the mouse wheel reaches. They are built once and owned, like a boat, rather than rolled like loot — there is nothing interesting about a rare scanner, and a Command Rod you might not have is the gate on the whole population system.

WHY THE FIRST TOOL IS FREE AND CHEAP. You START with a Knapped Tool. It used to cost stone, and stone comes off a rock, and a rock is tier 1 — which a bare-handed character cannot touch. So the cheapest tool in the game was behind a tool. It now costs only things hands can already take, and you are given one anyway, because a first hour spent unable to pick anything up is not a difficulty curve.

bases.name: Knapped Tool
bases.desc: A flaked head lashed to a cut haft. It digs clay and sand, cuts fibre and reed, and fells a young tree. Anything harder laughs at it.
bases.made: Lashed together out of what is lying about — no bench, no fire, nothing but your hands. Both of its materials come off things bare hands can already take (a dead tree, a bush), which is the point: it is the tool that unlocks every tool.

bases.name: Ironhead Pick and Axe
bases.desc: A proper head, both faces forged: a point for rock and a bit for timber. The tool the early game is balanced around.
bases.made: Forged at an anvil from iron ingots, which means a furnace and a seam first.

bases.name: Steelhead Pick and Axe
bases.desc: Hardened faces that hold an edge in deep vein, crystal and obsidian. This is the tier that opens the second half of the material table — and the one a meteor crater is waiting for.
bases.made: Forged at an anvil from steel, which comes off an Alloy Forge.

bases.name: Powered Cutter
bases.desc: A cutting head on a cell. It takes a gas vent and a rare seam, and it does in one pass what the steel head does in three.
bases.made: Assembled at a workbench. Parts, wire and a crystal — by which point you should be building drills instead.

devices.name: Prospector's Scanner
devices.desc: Sweeps the ground around you and names what is under it. What it finds stays on your map for good — it is a survey, not a torch.
devices.made: Built at a workbench. One crystal, a little wire and three iron.

devices.name: Deep Scanner
devices.desc: Twice the reach of the prospector's set and it reads through rock — the buried veins a hand scanner walks straight over.
devices.made: Built at a workbench once you are forging steel. It supersedes the first scanner rather than replacing it in the bag: the wheel holds one scanner, and it is the best one you own.

devices.name: Survey Array
devices.desc: A shoulder rig that reads the whole valley and tells the difference between a seam and a rare seam without your having to stand on it.
devices.made: Built at a workbench. The end of prospecting on foot.

devices.name: Command Rod
devices.desc: Point it at your own people and they listen. Select one or several and give them somewhere to be and something to do.
devices.made: Built at a workbench once you have a holding worth giving orders in.

gather._doc: How long a gather takes before it pays, in seconds, divided by the tool's speed. A seam is slower than a bush on purpose — hand mining is meant to be the thing that gets a drill built, not a career. "The goal isn't really to mine resources by hand, other than to get production started, it's really to build drills and automate a factory."
gather._moveCancelDoc: Walk this far from where you started and the bar drops. Small enough that you cannot wander off and still be gathering, big enough that a slope you slide down does not cancel it.

scan._doc: The scanner sweeps on a clock rather than every frame: a sweep walks the node field near you, and anything inside the range is remembered for the rest of the save. The range is deliberately short — "The scanner should only work nearby the player but once a node is scanned it should remain visible on the map."
